entry.idea: Hospitals and fusion researchers both need rare isotopes that are scarce and hard to get, so StandardX is building a refinery in the UK to produce them domestically.
entry.lesson: If two separate, growing industries depend on the same scarce raw material, one factory can serve both markets at once.
entry.name: StandardX

growth.reason: It just launched with its first funding round, so there are no output or revenue numbers yet.

market.reason: Rare isotopes are essential inputs for two big, growing fields, cancer treatment and nuclear fusion energy, though the product itself is a specialised industrial material rather than a mass consumer good.

tech.reason: Building an isotope refinery needs rare nuclear engineering know-how and specialised hardware that most companies cannot quickly copy.

entry.twist: The same refinery and process can supply isotopes to two very different customers at once, cancer-treatment centres and nuclear-fusion companies.
entry.who_pays: Hospitals and medical suppliers buying isotopes for cancer treatment, and fusion companies buying isotopes for their reactors.
entry.why_now: Global supplies of medical and fusion isotopes are tight and unreliable, just as demand from cancer care and the growing fusion industry is rising.
